patients.label: Man aged 27 years with progressive dysphonia, laryngeal MALT lymphoma and laryngeal amyloidosis treated with radiotherapy

identity_evidence.quote: A male patient, 27 years old, presented with progressive dysphonia for four years.

attribution_limitations: The CT of the cervical region is described only as seen "in previous examinations"; the source gives no date and does not say whether it preceded the four years of drug treatments or only the visit to the authors' service. No order is inferred.

The sentence lists "immunophenotyping, bone marrow immunohistochemistry and histopathology" together; it is unclear whether bone marrow modifies immunophenotyping and histopathology. No specimen is assigned to those two results.
"Signs of chronic laryngitis" is a videolaryngoscopy finding, not a stated diagnosis, so it is kept as an observation and not as a condition.
The staging result (for example an Ann Arbor stage) is not stated for this patient; only the PET-CT findings are given, so no stage or disease extent is recorded.

PET-CT, axial section of the cervical region. Discrete asymmetric radioconcentration.

claims.text: A 27-year-old man presented with progressive dysphonia for four years. During this period, several drug treatments, including antibiotics and systemic and inhaled corticosteroids, were unsuccessful, and he refused a biopsy. After further deterioration of the vocal quality he came to the authors' service. Videolaryngoscopy showed diffuse infiltration of the glottic and supraglottic regions with signs of chronic laryngitis, and there were no alterations in the cervical ganglionary chains. The discussion states that he was immunocompetent and had no diagnosis of autoimmune disease.

claims.text: Computed tomography of the cervical region in previous examinations showed diffuse mucosal thickening of the larynx and cervical tracheal segment with obliteration of the paraglottic and pre-epiglottic fat planes, and laboratory tests showed no alterations. Biopsy at direct laryngoscopy showed amyloidosis with lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate in the right vocal fold, and immunohistochemistry was compatible with MALT lymphoma. The myelogram showed an increased erythrocyte series, and PET-CT showed slight asymmetric radioconcentration with a grade 3 Deauville score.
